Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. As promised, I pulled together a short proposal for an annual commit structure that Horizon can use to smooth unit economics while keeping a clear fallback to PAYG if usage is variable in the early months. Attached is a one-page summary and the draft terms.

High level (Starter / Growth / Enterprise):
- Starter: 10M tokens/yr — baseline 20% off list per-token for the first year; overage at 1.15x committed unit price.
- Growth: 50M tokens/yr — baseline 30% off; 10% buffer that can be applied as short-term burst at committed price.
- Enterprise: 200M tokens/yr — baseline 40% off; roll-forward of up to 10% unused tokens in Q1 + priority routing and predictable latency SLA.

Safety-valve idea: if monthly usage exceeds committed burn by more than buffer, customer can either (a) pay overage at a reduced premium to avoid throttles, or (b) convert to a short-term addendum to increase the committed tier with prorated credit. We designed two options because Horizon mentioned bursty promotional windows.

Attached: blended_commit_summary.xlsx (breakdown by effective $/1k tokens) and safety_valve_terms.pdf (term language snippet).

If this looks directionally right, I can loop Marissa for commercial and Karthik for technical pricing guarantees on quant/latency expectations. Would you like a 30-minute call Thursday to walk through numbers with finance?

Best,

Emily —

Quick answers, and I've added a simple worked example below. Happy to jump on a call Thursday afternoon.

1) Roll-forward: Starter tier — 25% of unused tokens can roll to the next quarter (not year). Growth/Enterprise get 10% roll-forward per quarter up to the end of year. This is intended to avoid heavy Q1 churn while keeping annual economics predictable.

2) Overage math (example): Starter list price baseline = $0.045 / 1k tokens (list). Starter committed price after 20% off = $0.036 / 1k tokens. If you exceed monthly committed burn by more than the 5% monthly buffer, overage would be charged at $0.045 / 1k (list) + 15% premium = $0.05175 / 1k tokens — we can alternatively offer a flat $0.050 / 1k if you prefer a round number.

3) Minimum term: 12 months standard; we can offer a 9-month pilot for Starter with pro-rata pricing and no early termination fee — good option if you want to validate promotions seasonality.

Worked example (Starter) — annual commit 10M tokens:
- Committed avg monthly burn = ~833k tokens.
- Month A uses 1.1M tokens (exceeds by ~267k). First 5% monthly buffer (~41k tokens) absorbed. Remaining 226k tokens -> overage charged at $0.05 /1k = $11.30 additional for that month.

I attached a spreadsheet tab with the monthly roll-forward calculator. If you want purely per-token math (no multipliers), we recommend the flat $0.050 /1k overage for simplicity.

Marissa Cole

Two quick technical guardrails from the pricing/ops side to make the commercial terms reliable in production: 

1) Transparent token accounting: we'll provide a token-by-route live dashboard and daily burn CSV export for Horizon's finance team. This will make overage alerts automated (threshold alerts at 80/90/100%).
2) Safety-valve capacity: when usage spikes we can optionally route excess traffic to a PAYG pool with best-effort latency; if Horizon needs committed latency guarantees during a promo, we recommend short-term commit addendum (prorated) rather than permanent overage pricing. The addendum workflow takes 24-48 hours to provision dedicated capacity but avoids headroom constraints.

Operational note: the roll-forward is an accounting policy only — we do not reserve extra tokens in infrastructure unless you choose a short addendum. That keeps costs predictable for both sides.

I can draft the short-term addendum language for approval. Also attaching the safety valve term snippet that Jordan included.
